issues.title: Invalid characteristic-patch volume estimate in Theorem 3.1
issues.failure_explanation: In theorem3.1, k≥2 and the unit direction are fixed while h tends to zero on quasi-uniform, shape-regular meshes, and the constants in ≲ must be independent of h. The set D_c is the union of full boundary elements touching the regular codimension-two characteristic set, rather than an h^k-thin mismatch region. In d=2, one nonempty regular characteristic point already gives Vol(D_c) bounded below by a constant times h²; in d=3, a characteristic curve of order-one length intersects order h^{-1} tetrahedra of volume order h³, again producing order h². This is incompatible with Vol(D_c) ≲ h^{k+1} for k≥2. Moreover, eq3.8 concerns the norm of tilde I minus its transformed counterpart and does not imply a volume estimate. With the actual patch scaling, the old trace calculation controls T3 only at order h^k, not the h^{k+1/2} required for the theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The boundary-consistency term T3 is not bounded at the rate required for eq3.18, so the old proof does not establish theorem3.1's optimal DG convergence estimate. The theorem is not thereby shown false, and no later formal result depends on it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace only the estimate of T3 and delete the false claim Vol(D_c) ≲ h^{k+1}. Let S = Γ_h^- \ Φ_h(Γ^-). The already established bounds give |S| ≲ h^k and |Ω·n_h| ≲ h^k on S. Hence, using the inverse trace estimate for v_h ∈ V_{h,k}, ||v_h||_{L²(S)} ≲ h^{-1/2}||v_h||_{DG}, one obtains |T3| ≲ h^k ||tilde I||_{L∞(Γ_h)} |S|^{1/2}||v_h||_{L²(S)} ≲ h^{3k/2-1/2}||tilde I||_{L∞(Γ_h)}||v_h||_{DG}. Since k ≥ 2, this is at most order h^{k+1/2}; the original W^{1,∞} hypothesis controls the required L∞ norm. Thus Theorem 3.1 and its stated optimal rate can be retained unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The volume estimate is genuinely false and is used in an invalid inference, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, the theorem is recovered with the same hypotheses, conclusion, and convergence rate by a short local replacement using the paper's existing symmetric-difference and normal estimates together with standard Hölder and inverse-trace inequalities. No new lemma, proof architecture, or weakening of the result is required.
